about: The allowed exceptions of the import-rules ratchet (packages/core/test/import-rules.test.ts, rules in scripts/audit/lib.mjs). Each group has one rule, a one-line reason and its entries ("<file> → <import>"). A new entry and a stale one both fail the test: after a change, run node scripts/audit/rules.mjs . --write-baseline, write the reason of any new group, and review the diff.

groups.reason: CLI commands read and write files or start processes themselves (ui) until they go through the engine.
The Studio server watches folders, serves files and supervises its worker itself.

Shell sources outside the commands, tools and the Studio server, real machine work of the shell itself: the MCP HTTP port holder (its lock file, and `ps` for the process that holds the port: the shell's own listener), the Studio's esbuild bundler of its app (reads its own app sources) and the player's bundler (reads its own frame sources and the Player's version; which components it bundles, their hashes, the composition and the import rules come from the engine).

Real value dependencies, kept on purpose: the editor is the renderer of the component system — it bundles a workspace's component folders with the kit and the geometry entry (render/bundle.ts: the component files' layout, manifests, unhashed-file rules, kit and geometry entry paths), its compositions draw with the kit's Logo, Wordmark and backgroundCss (remotion/PlanVideo.tsx, Preview.tsx: bundled code, so a port cannot hand them), a component preview fills its slots and samples with the components' layout maths (preview.ts, render/preview.ts: source hashes, preview README blocks; render/preview-session.ts, the preview session split out of render/preview.ts: the component system's themeTokens and paramDefaults fill a previewed component's theme and params, the same dependency as its file's); the sandbox reads where a database URL connects with the hooks' one reader of it (`@retake/hooks/db-url`: pg's parser, it never connects; not a domain entry because it loads pg). A plan, a render and a review load no registry: the engine hands it (its ComponentRegistries port).

Two imports of a later context, measured when the contexts were drawn: the scenario's checks read the default theme's component names (template-defaults, theme) to check a scenario's components, and a script's draft checks its page paths with the inspection's grammar (inspectPathProblem, run). Each goes when that value moves below the scenario context.
The journal's warn rate limit (append-log.ts logWarner): a process-wide helper with no clock in reach, compared with itself, never written; its test moves Date.now.
Memo lifetimes kept in memory only (the board's and the scenario view's caches, the Studio's one-time bootstrap codes): compared with the time they were made, never written.
File times: a filming marker's heartbeat and the library cache's recency are compared with the mtimes other processes leave, so they follow the machine's own time.
Outside the engine's contexts: the app set-up (`retake app`, the desktop app) has no composition root of the engine; its backup name takes an injectable `now` already.
agent-written.ts reads the workspaces of an agent's write and a scenario's hooks for `retake hooks trust` on core io's loaders: the file is not on the port yet and goes onto it in a later change

The Studio's own ops (18 in 6 files on 2026-11-12; 19 since desktop_menu, 2026-11-15; 25 since the app's Tools, 2026-11-17: they hold the set-up gate, the download this server runs and its last check): every use case the engine serves is its operation now; these hold the server's own state (its index, player, leases, set-up and update state, unsaved tabs, the desktop pipe) and stay here.
Test defaults of the job queue adapters' constructors (the roots hand theirs through the ports' queue factory, as with their clock).

This process's own environment, on purpose: the captures folder's test-run guard reads it beside the environment handed (a test that hands a clean one still never uses the per-user folder); the two `ps` runs get it with the C locale (a subprocess inherits this process's environment; yield.ts parses the start times `ps` prints in this process's time zone).

Paths spelt as text on purpose: the trust lists (agent-writable paths, a person's files), a new project's .gitignore lines, help texts and the Studio's browser code (no node:path there), and the app bundle's first module's copy of the Retake home (core io bundle.ts homeFolder: it imports node: builtins only, pinned against retakeHome by a test).

Other names with a grammar of the same shape, each written at its definition and out of the id module: a scenario name (SLUG_RE), a project slug (PROJECT_SLUG_RE), a run-folder segment, a review file id.
The file suffixes of the export formats (`<render id>-vertical.mp4`, `-square.mp4`), not the variant suffix of a render id.
The new-theme grammar without its cap, on purpose: the names inside stale work folders of earlier theme creations, which must be cleaned whatever their length.
The shared home helper's own test (the canary of the test environment): it keeps the run's home by hand, so that a broken helper cannot leave its own test's home behind.
entries: packages/core/test/retake-home.test.ts → 1 hand-written RETAKE_HOME save or restore

groups.reason: Prune reads the run folders through the reader and keeps its lenient read for one case: a run.json the reader does not take as a record (a finished run without its end, a failed one without its error, a linked file) is still read as any object with a text id and status, so that a take prune could delete with its earlier rules can still be deleted — leaving such a take alone is a change nobody decided. Where this read is stricter than before it only keeps: a file of a newer format is left alone, one that is no regular file or is over the reader's cap is not read. Its second read is of renders/: a record file that is a link is not opened by the one reader of renders/, and is read through the link for the id, the take, the scenario and the creation time it says — never taken as a record — so that a linked record keeps the render and the take it kept with the earlier rules.
entries: packages/engine/src/prune.ts → 2 own reads of a run folder's or renders/'s file

groups.reason: A reserved run is closed from outside on a lenient read of its run.json (its status alone decides): a record the reader refuses must still be closed, or it would say running for ever.
